facts.statement: Thanatotheristes lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically between 80.1 and 79.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: approximately 80.1-79.5 Ma

facts.statement: Fossils of Thanatotheristes have been found in the Foremost Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Foremost Formation of Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: A referred specimen was discovered at the Twelve Mile Coulee within the upper Herronton Sandstone of the Foremost Formation.
facts.quote: Twelve Mile Coulee in the upper Herronton Sandstone of the Foremost Formation

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype individual has been estimated to be approximately 800 mm in length.
facts.quote: The length of the skull has been approximated to be 800 mm

facts.statement: The holotype individual was not osteologically mature when it died.
facts.quote: not osteologically mature at the time of death

facts.statement: The type specimen of Thanatotheristes is estimated to have reached a length of 8 meters.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Thanatotheristes has been estimated at 8 m

facts.statement: Thanatotheristes is characterized by a single row of evenly spaced ridges on the underside of the maxilla near the antorbital fossa.
facts.quote: A single row of evenly spaced dorsoventrally oriented ridges on the subcutaneous surface of the maxilla ventral and anteroventral to the antorbital fossa

facts.statement: The frontal bone features a sagittal crest that extends forward of the supratemporal ridge as a broad, rounded structure.
facts.quote: Sagittal crest on the frontal extends anterior to the supratemporal ridge as a broad and rounded ridge

facts.statement: The prefrontal bone has two prongs that project backward and connect with the frontal bone on the underside of the skull roof.
facts.quote: Prefrontal with two posteriorly projecting prongs articulating with the frontal on ventral surface of skull roof

facts.statement: The description of Thanatotheristes led to the establishment of the new clade Daspletosaurini within Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: erected a new clade within Tyrannosauridae, Daspletosaurini

facts.statement: The existence of Daspletosaurini indicates geographic segregation of tyrannosaurid clades, with some groups living in southern Laramidia and others in Canada and northern USA.
facts.quote: shows that there is geographic segregation of clades within Tyrannosauridae

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest that the unique features of the frontal bone might be inadequate, potentially making Thanatotheristes a species of Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: This may suggest that any autapomorphies or synapomorphies pertaining to the frontal of T. degrootorum are inadequate, and may therefore render it a species of Daspletosaurus

facts.statement: Thanatotheristes lived alongside medium-sized ceratopsids and small pachycephalosaurids.
facts.quote: coexisting with medium-sized ceratopsids like Xenoceratops foremostensis and small pachycephalosaurids like Colepiocephale lambei

facts.statement: Thanatotheristes was significantly smaller than its close relative, Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: era significativamente más pequeño que el de su taxón hermano, Daspletosaurus

facts.statement: Thanatotheristes degrootorum belongs to the tribe Daspletosaurini, which is a sister taxon to Tyrannosaurini within the family Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: La descripción formal de T. degrootorum erigió una nueva tribu dentro de Tyrannosauridae, Daspletosaurini, un taxón hermano de Tyrannosaurini.

facts.statement: The tribe Daspletosaurini is diagnosed by features including a thick subcutaneous surface on the anterior ventral maxilla, a narrow jugal ramus, a maxillary angle less than 65 degrees, a broad and dorsomedially arched prefrontal, a dental chin ventral to the third alveolus, and at least 14 maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: Daspletosaurini se diagnostica por las siguientes características La presencia de una superficie subcutánea extremadamente gruesa del maxilar anteroventral a la fosa antorbital, una rama yugal estrecha del maxilar, la esquina anteroventral del maxilar se estrecha en un ángulo poco profundo (<65 °) medido entre el margen alveolar de los dos primeros alvéolos y el margen anterior de la superficie subcutánea, un prefrontal que es amplio en la vista dorsal y fuertemente arqueado dorsomedialmente en la vista anterior,un mentón dentario ubicado ventral al tercer alveolo o la tercera placa interdental y poseen no menos de 14 dientes maxilares.

facts.statement: A 2020 analysis by Yun suggested that diagnostic features of tyrannosaurid taxa might be inadequate due to wide morphological ranges in frontal bones, potentially invalidating the separation of Thanatotheristes.
facts.quote: Un análisis del hueso frontal de un ejemplar subadulto de Daspletosaurus torosus publicado por Yun, 2020 sugiere que las características de este hueso demostrarían que efectivamente las autapomorfias de algunos taxones de tiranosáuridos serían inadecuadas, debido al amplio de rango de morfología en los frontales dentro de clados particulares.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Thanatotheristes is the tribe Daspletosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Daspletosaurini

facts.statement: Thanatotheristes is classified within the family Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Tyrannosauridae

facts.statement: Thanatotheristes is classified under the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Thanatotheristes is Thanatotheristes degrootorum.
facts.quote: Type species: Thanatotheristes degrootorum

facts.statement: Thanatotheristes lived during the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Thanatotheristes in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2
